chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

A resident should not lead a traveler, nor should a traveler lead a resident. If one is tried with something of that, and he leads resident people, then when he completes the two rak'ahs he gives salām, then takes one of them by the hand and puts him forward, and he leads them. And when the traveler prays behind resident people, then let him complete his prayer as two rak'ahs and give salām. And if he prays al-zuhr with them, then let him make the first two al-zuhr and the last two al-'asr.
So the correct understanding regarding these two reports is a degree of dislike short of prohibition, according to what he عليه السلام detailed of its rulings.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of salat (prayer) performed by the traveler
key_terms.الْحَضَرِيُّ: a resident person, as opposed to a traveler
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness in legal ruling, short of prohibition
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: a traveler subject to shortened salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: he gave the salām ending the salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads others in congregational salat (prayer) as Imam

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler and a resident lead one another in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings related to congregational salat (prayer) between a traveler and a resident. It explains how the prayer is to be completed when such a situation occurs, and the closing note states that the apparent ruling in these reports indicates karahah (dislikedness), not prohibition.
